scope: Dinner Roulette physical casino destinations; destination-scale tribal casinos are in scope, while ordinary travel plazas, smoke shops, convenience outlets and duplicated regulator rows require explicit exclusion or separate destination justification
auditDecision: Oklahoma is too large and structurally noisy for a one-shot catalog pass. Audit by tribal/operator cluster, preserve regulator rows as evidence, and only promote separately routable destination casinos after scope, identity, address and coordinate QA.
knownStructuralIssues: The federal gaming roster mixes destination casinos with travel plazas, smoke-shop casinos, trading-post gaming and other smaller gaming outlets.
Some tribes operate multiple casino brands and multiple separately located properties under the same brand family.
The same physical address or tribal administrative address may appear across more than one federal roster row; regulator-row count must not be treated as runtime destination count.
Current branding can differ from historical federal roster naming, so current tribal/operator first-party sources are required before runtime activation.
Class II-only properties can still qualify when they are clearly promoted and operated as destination casinos; gaming class alone is not the Dinner Roulette scope test.
